title: Space Bound for Oracle Register Programs
statement: Let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let a nondeterministic register program with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle languages have a finite control-state set with decidable equality. Let $S,W:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $C$ be a natural number, with $1\le S(n)$ and $W(n)\le C S(n)$ for every $n$. Suppose each oracle language $A_j$ is decided by a deterministic machine using at most $s_j(n)$ space on inputs of length $n$. Assume that whenever $v\le 2n+2+m(2W(n)+2)$, one has $s_j(v)\le C S(n)$ for every $j,n$. For some input-independent natural bound $N$ (which may depend on the input), suppose that on each input $x$ every choice string of length $N$ makes the program halt, and every configuration before step $N$ satisfies the program's validity conditions and has each register's binary representation of its value plus one of length at most $W(|x|)$. If $x\in L$ exactly when some length-$N$ choice string makes the program answer yes, then $L$ belongs to $	ext{NSPACE}(S)$: it is decidable in nondeterministic space bounded by a constant multiple of $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of binary strings
The program has $m$ registers and $d$ oracle languages
The finite control-state set has decidable equality
Each oracle language $A_j$ has a deterministic decider using space $s_j$
For each input, some length $N$ makes every choice string of that length halt
Every pre-final run configuration satisfies the program's validity conditions
Each register's binary representation of its value plus one has length at most $W(|x|)$
Membership in $L$ is equivalent to existence of a length-$N$ accepting choice string
